summary: Settings-style navigation surface with a native destination link, optional supporting copy, a fixed ChevronRight affordance, and an optional application-owned body.
useWhen: A settings page needs a card that leads to a deeper settings destination.
A compact destination card needs the complete surface to act as one link.
A settings summary must remain visible in a body while only the card header navigates.
avoidWhen: The card edits its contents in place; use CardSetting for the edit-save-cancel workflow.
The destination is an action without a navigable URL.
The surface contains a chart, legend, metric visualization, or other data-visualization composition.

alternatives.when: The section switches between read-only and editable content in place.
alternatives.reason: CardSetting owns the controlled edit-save-cancel workflow.

alternatives.when: The surface contains a chart or specialized data-visualization composition.
alternatives.reason: CardChart owns the independently evolving chart-card contract.

accessibility: CardNavigation renders a native link whenever href resolves to an allowed URL, so Enter activation, link context menus, and modified-click behavior remain available.
The heading is rendered as an h2 and the optional description contributes to the link's accessible name.
The ChevronRight icon is decorative because the link text already names the destination.
Use the content variant only when interactive body content must remain outside the header link; never place interactive descendants inside the navigation-only card.
dsNavigate is cancelable so client-side routers can prevent native navigation after accepting an unmodified activation.
states: The native link owns hover, pressed, and focus-visible states across the complete card in navigation-only mode.
In content mode, the native link owns those interaction states only across the header while the body remains application-owned.
An empty or unsafe href renders non-interactive card chrome without a false keyboard target.
The application owns destination loading, authorization, not-found, and recovery states after navigation.
responsiveBehavior: Choose sm, md, or lg from the parent layout; the surface never exceeds its parent width.
Supporting copy wraps while the chevron remains visible at the trailing edge.
The parent owns wrapping, columns, stacking, and breakpoint changes between cards.

customElements: Set href to a valid relative or HTTP(S) URL.
Prevent dsNavigate only when an application router takes ownership of the same activation.
react: Pass href for native link semantics and use onDsNavigate only when coordinating with a client-side router.
Use variant content when projecting interactive body content so those controls stay outside the link.
angular: Bind href and prevent dsNavigate before calling Router.navigateByUrl for unmodified primary activations.
Use variant content when projecting interactive body content so those controls stay outside the link.
